## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

subject_definitions

<Subject 1> is the male model from <Picture 1>.
Use <Picture 1> ONLY as a human identity and body reference.
Preserve only the model's body proportions, neck structure, shoulders, arms, hands, skin tone, posture tendency, and overall mature male fashion-model presence.

IMPORTANT:
The clothing visible in <Picture 1> is completely irrelevant and must be ignored.
Do NOT inherit, preserve, blend, copy, transfer, or reference any clothing information from <Picture 1>, including but not limited to:
- color
- brightness
- saturation
- fabric texture
- collar shape
- neckline
- sleeve length
- garment silhouette
- buttons
- placket
- folds
- seam structure
- style category
- layering logic

<Subject 2> is the target men's jacket defined ONLY by <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>.
<Picture 2> is the ONLY authoritative source for the FRONT view of the jacket.
<Picture 3> is the ONLY authoritative source for the BACK view of the jacket.

All garment-related information must come exclusively from <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>, including:
- color family
- hue
- brightness
- material appearance
- silhouette
- collar construction
- zipper structure
- pocket placement
- sleeve pocket design
- cuffs
- hem
- seams
- proportions
- internal visible structure if naturally exposed by the jacket

<Picture 2> and <Picture 3> describe the same physical jacket.
The jacket must remain fully consistent during motion and body rotation.

summary

[reference generation]
Create a premium 15-second vertical menswear product-commercial video in 9:16 format.

The male model from <Picture 1> is wearing the target jacket defined by <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>.
The purpose of the video is to clearly showcase the jacket on a real male model in a luxury hotel lobby / business-travel setting.

The video should feel like a refined menswear commercial:
mature,
masculine,
premium,
business casual,
modern urban lifestyle,
high-end fashion advertising.

The video should focus on:
1. a strong front-view introduction,
2. elegant walking movement in a premium hotel space,
3. clear collar / zipper / front-structure visibility,
4. sleeve-pocket detail showcase,
5. a natural body turn revealing the back,
6. a final front-facing hero shot.

retention_analysis

<Subject 1> retention:
Preserve the male model identity and human body traits from <Picture 1>, including:
- body build
- shoulder width
- neck and jaw area proportions
- arm shape
- hand structure
- skin tone
- natural masculine presence

Do NOT preserve the original upper-body clothing from <Picture 1> in any way.

FULL GARMENT REPLACEMENT IS MANDATORY:
The original upper-body clothing visible in <Picture 1> must be completely removed and fully replaced by the target jacket from <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>.

This is NOT:
- a recolor
- a partial edit
- a style transfer
- a hybrid garment
- a layering task

This IS:
- a full clothing replacement task

Do not preserve any part of the original shirt from <Picture 1>, including:
- polo collar
- neckline
- placket
- buttons
- chest opening
- sleeve edges
- shirt color
- inner shirt logic
- any visible shirt remains

NO ORIGINAL INNER SHIRT MAY REMAIN VISIBLE:
Do not leave any visible remains of the original clothing from <Picture 1> at:
- neck opening
- chest opening
- collar area
- shoulder edge
- sleeve opening
- hem area

Do not show a separate T-shirt, polo shirt, undershirt, or inner top unless it is explicitly supported by the garment references.
If the jacket is slightly open, the visible inner area must follow the jacket's authentic internal structure from <Picture 2>/<Picture 3>, not the original clothing from <Picture 1>.

<Subject 2> retention:
Preserve the jacket with very high product fidelity.
The jacket must match <Picture 2> for front-facing views and <Picture 3> for back-facing views.

STRICT SOURCE SEPARATION:
<Picture 1> contributes ONLY the human model.
<Picture 2>/<Picture 3> contribute ALL clothing information.

COLOR IS A HARD CONSTRAINT:
The final worn jacket must preserve the exact color direction, material feel, and visual logic of the jacket shown in <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>.

Under no circumstances may the model use, blend, sample, inherit, approximate, or transfer the clothing color from <Picture 1>.

The original green shirt color from <Picture 1> must NOT influence the jacket in any way.
Do not tint the jacket toward green.
Do not preserve the original shirt’s color logic.
Do not mix the original shirt tone into the jacket body, collar, cuffs, sleeves, shadows, highlights, folds, or hem.

If any conflict exists between <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>/<Picture 3>, always discard all clothing information from <Picture 1> and strictly follow <Picture 2>/<Picture 3>.

Do not invent extra garment elements.
Do not hallucinate:
- extra logos
- extra text
- extra pockets
- extra straps
- extra zippers
- new decorations
- new patches
- new layers
- unsupported inner garments

Negative constraints:
- do not keep the original polo-shirt color
- do not keep the original polo-shirt collar
- do not preserve the original neckline from <Picture 1>
- do not create a hybrid between the original shirt and the target jacket
- do not create layered clothing unless clearly supported by the jacket references
- do not reveal an inner T-shirt or polo
- do not mix the original shirt into the jacket
- do not reinterpret the jacket into another color palette
- do not generate a jacket that still feels like the shirt from <Picture 1>

detailed_description

[Shot 1 | 0.0s - 2.0s]
A premium medium waist-up shot inside an upscale modern hotel lobby.
<Subject 1> is already fully wearing <Subject 2>.
The original clothing from <Picture 1> must be completely absent.
The jacket front must strictly follow <Picture 2>.
No visible polo collar, no undershirt neckline, no original shirt remains.
The model stands calmly near a large floor-to-ceiling window or elegant stone wall.
Warm architectural indoor light combines with soft natural window light.
The camera performs a slow elegant push-in.
The jacket is the primary visual focus.

[Shot 2 | 2.0s - 4.2s]
The model begins walking slowly and naturally through the luxury hotel lobby.
Use a medium shot with smooth side tracking.
The movement is restrained, confident, and premium.
Clearly show the front silhouette of the jacket while walking.
The jacket front must remain faithful to <Picture 2>.
Natural walking motion should create realistic folds in the body and sleeves.
Do not reveal any original clothing from <Picture 1>.

[Shot 3 | 4.2s - 6.3s]
A closer chest-level tracking shot.
Focus on the collar construction, zipper area, upper chest structure, and fabric surface.
The model continues a very gentle slow walk or a subtle pause.
Show the jacket’s materials and stitching clearly.
All visible front-side details must strictly follow <Picture 2>.
No green tint.
No shirt neckline.
No hybrid layering.

[Shot 4 | 6.3s - 8.5s]
A controlled product detail close-up of the sleeve and utility-pocket area.
The model makes one small natural arm movement, such as slightly lifting the forearm or adjusting posture.
Show the sleeve pocket structure, zipper, stitching, seam behavior, and fabric volume clearly.
Use shallow depth of field.
The hotel environment stays softly blurred.
Do not invent extra hardware or design changes.

[Shot 5 | 8.5s - 10.8s]
Return to a medium shot near a refined hotel passage or window area.
The model stops walking and slowly rotates his torso and upper body from the front toward the side and then toward the back.
This is one continuous, smooth, natural turn.
The jacket must remain consistent during the transition.
Front-facing clothing information follows <Picture 2>, and rear-facing clothing information gradually transitions toward <Picture 3>.
Do not allow the original clothing from <Picture 1> to reappear during motion.

[Shot 6 | 10.8s - 12.8s]
The model now clearly presents the back of the jacket.
The back must accurately follow <Picture 3>.
Show the rear collar, shoulder structure, back panel, sleeve silhouette, hem, and overall back proportions clearly.
Use a slight lateral camera move or a very subtle follow movement.
Warm hotel lighting outlines the garment silhouette.
Keep the shot elegant and restrained.

[Shot 7 | 12.8s - 15.0s]
The model smoothly turns back into a three-quarter front hero pose.
The front appearance must return strictly to <Picture 2>.
He performs one subtle premium menswear gesture, such as lightly adjusting the collar or touching the front edge of the jacket.
Do not perform multiple gestures at once.
No original shirt may appear.
End on a stable waist-up hero shot.
The final frame should clearly showcase the jacket silhouette, collar, front structure, sleeves, and overall masculine fit.

overall_visual_direction

Premium luxury hotel menswear campaign.
Modern business travel lifestyle.
Mature masculine aesthetic.
High-end commercial photography.
Warm architectural lighting.
Soft natural window light.
Subtle cinematic contrast.
Polished stone.
Dark wood.
Brushed metal.
Minimal luxury interiors.
Realistic skin.
Realistic fabric.
Natural clothing folds.
Shallow depth of field.
Restrained camera movement.
Clean composition.

The environment must support the garment and never overpower it.
The jacket must always remain the visual priority.

camera_language

Use mostly medium shots, waist-up shots, chest-level close-ups, and garment detail close-ups.
Use slow dolly movement, smooth side tracking, subtle arc tracking during rotation, and precise detail close-ups.
No handheld shake.
No fast camera movement.
No rapid zooms.
No unstable motion.
No exaggerated slow motion.
Avoid wide shots unless the jacket remains clearly visible.

overall_soundscape

Quiet premium hotel ambience.
Subtle indoor space tone, faint distant environmental presence, and gentle fabric rustling when the model walks, turns, or lightly adjusts the jacket.
No dialogue.
No narration.
No loud transition effects.

non_diegetic_music

A premium modern menswear commercial instrumental.
Tempo around 95-105 BPM.
Minimal deep percussion.
Subtle bass.
Refined modern electronic texture.
Sophisticated, understated, masculine, and contemporary.
No vocals.
The music should support the clean pacing of the fashion showcase, build slightly during the walking and rotation section, and resolve calmly during the final hero shot.

FINAL HARD RULES:

This is a full clothing replacement task.
The model from <Picture 1> must wear ONLY the jacket defined by <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>.

The original upper-body clothing from <Picture 1> must be completely removed and must never remain visible.

Do not show:
- the original polo collar
- any undershirt neckline
- any original shirt opening
- any original garment color influence
- any layered-shirt effect

Only the target jacket may appear as the visible upper-body garment.

If ambiguity occurs, prioritize garment fidelity over stylistic creativity.
If ambiguity occurs, discard all clothing information from <Picture 1>.
